However, coronary angiography or myocardial perfusion imaging has not returned results, so obstructive coronary artery disease is not directly confirmed. Therefore, confidence in coronary artery disease with exercise-induced myocardial ischemia is increased from 0.70 to 0.75.

node-14.label: Coronary angiography or myocardial perfusion imaging was requested but no results are available

node-15.label: Aortic valve sclerosis with mild regurgitation contributes to exertional dyspnea

attrs.why: Echocardiography shows a sclerotic aortic valve with mild regurgitation, a structural cardiac abnormality that can contribute to exertional dyspnea. However, expert analyses emphasize that this finding does not explain the dynamic QRS widening and new T-wave inversions, and it is considered an additional contributor rather than the primary cause. Confidence is therefore low at 0.3.

node-16.label: Coronary artery disease with exercise-induced myocardial ischemia

attrs.why: The current frontier 'Cardiac disease (CAD/HF)' is too broad. The exercise ECG showing dynamic QRS widening and new T-wave inversions in recovery (node-10) strongly supports exercise-induced myocardial ischemia. Normal BNP, preserved LVEF, no wall motion abnormalities, and resting narrow QRS (nodes 8, 9, 13) argue against heart failure, making CAD with ischemia the most plausible specific refinement.

node-17.label: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)

attrs.why: This refines the broad cardiac disease frontier by considering a heart failure subtype. However, normal BNP, preserved LVEF, no wall motion abnormalities, and narrow QRS (nodes 8, 9, 13) substantially reduce the likelihood of HFpEF, and it does not explain the ischemic exercise ECG changes (node-10).

node-18.label: Aortic valve sclerosis with hemodynamically significant regurgitation as primary cause

attrs.why: This refines the cardiac disease frontier by evaluating valvular heart disease. Echocardiography shows sclerotic aortic valve with mild regurgitation (node-11), but expert analyses indicate this does not explain the dynamic QRS widening and T-wave inversions (node-10), so it is only a minor contributor rather than the primary cause.
